# Results — Study 359 (Farmland)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The "farmland is the best inflation
hedge" claim, tested three ways: (1) the only **tradable** farmland exposure — the listed REITs
**LAND** and **FPI** — regressed against **SPY**; (2) a **cited public NCREIF Farmland Index**
annual series (appraisal-based, 1992–2023) regressed against **CPI**; (3) the appraisal-smoothing
that makes the NCREIF numbers look so calm. Listed-proxy numbers use yfinance auto-adjusted month-
end closes; the NCREIF/CPI/S&P annual series is hardcoded (cited public figures); the synthetic
control is deterministic. Run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Listed proxies | yfinance auto-adjusted month-end closes — LAND, FPI, SPY |
| Window (proxies) | 2014-02-28 → 2026-06-30 (LAND n=149, FPI n=146 months) |
| Appraisal index | NCREIF Farmland Index annual total return, **hardcoded cited public series**, 1992–2023 (n=32) |
| Inflation / market | BLS CPI-U + S&P 500 annual total return, same years (hardcoded, cited) |
| As-of | 2026-06-22 |

> **Scope caveats (named on the axes).** *Signal* — the tradable proxies are a **12-year, 2-name**
> sample (survivorship: both REITs survived; a third that delisted would not appear). The NCREIF
> inflation regression is **32 annual points** — low power. *Tradability* — LAND/FPI are small,
> **leveraged**, thinly-traded REITs; the smooth NCREIF risk is **not** the risk you bear. The
> NCREIF series is a **cited public proxy** for the paywalled quarterly index, not the index itself.

## Half 1 — the tradable proxies are NOT low-beta diversifiers

The only farmland you can actually buy is equity-like and market-correlated — the opposite of the
"uncorrelated, low-vol" pitch. CAPM beta vs SPY, monthly, HAC (6-lag) *t*:

| proxy | n | ann. return | ann. vol | market beta (HAC t) | corr to SPY | alpha/yr (t) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **LAND** (Gladstone Land) | 149 | +4.9% | **30.0%** | **0.91** (t = 5.19) | 0.44 | −8.2% (t = −1.03) |
| **FPI** (Farmland Partners) | 146 | +5.5% | **29.3%** | **0.69** (t = 4.11) | 0.35 | −4.3% (t = −0.59) |
| SPY (benchmark) | 149 | +14.4% | 14.6% | 1.00 | 1.00 | — |

Listed farmland carries **~30% annual volatility** (double the S&P) and a **significant ~0.7–0.9
market beta**. There is no positive alpha (point estimates negative, insignificant). The calm,
uncorrelated picture lives only in the appraisal index, not in any vehicle you can hold.

## Half 2 — the inflation-hedge claim is real-but-weak (insignificant)

NCREIF farmland annual total return regressed on CPI (HAC), 1992–2023:

| asset | mean | vol | corr to CPI | inflation-beta (HAC t) | mean real return |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **NCREIF farmland** | 11.0% | 6.6% | +0.14 | **+0.66 (t = 0.83)** | **+8.4%/yr** |
| S&P 500 | 11.6% | 17.7% | −0.33 | −3.98 (t = −2.69) | — |

Farmland's inflation loading is **positive but statistically insignificant** (t = 0.83 on 32 years),
while equities load **negatively** on inflation. So farmland *is* the better inflation companion of
the two — and earns a high +8.4%/yr real return — but the inflation-hedge coefficient itself **does
not clear the t ≥ 2 bar** on the real tape. Real economic story, weak statistical proof: **WEAK**.

## Half 3 — "smooth & uncorrelated" is an appraisal artifact (BUSTED)

The NCREIF series reports lag-1 autocorrelation **ρ₁ = 0.63** — a fingerprint of appraisal smoothing
(true asset returns are near-zero autocorrelated). Un-smoothing (Geltner first-order reversal):

| | reported | un-smoothed |
|---|--:|--:|
| NCREIF farmland annual vol | **6.6%** | **13.5%** |

Removing the smoothing **doubles** the volatility (ratio 0.49) — the appraisal process hides ~51% of
the real risk. The "low-vol, near-zero-correlation" property is manufactured by the measurement, not
a feature of the asset. The synthetic positive control proves the mechanism exactly:

| smoothing a | var-ratio (measured / closed-form a/(2−a)) | ρ₁ (measured / 1−a) | true beta → appraised |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.10 | 0.048 / 0.053 | 0.888 / 0.900 | 0.32 → **0.03** |
| 0.20 | 0.105 / 0.111 | 0.786 / 0.800 | 0.32 → **0.06** |
| 0.40 | 0.246 / 0.250 | 0.591 / 0.600 | 0.32 → **0.13** |

A true beta of 0.32 is reported as **0.03–0.13** purely because the index is appraised — exactly the
"farmland barely moves with the market" illusion. The engine recovers the closed-form shrink to
Monte-Carlo error.

## Tradability — costs on NAV

Buy-and-hold net Sharpe (15 bps one-way; LAND/FPI are small, leveraged, thin):

| proxy | gross Sharpe | net Sharpe | ann. vol |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| LAND | 0.16 | 0.16 | 30.0% |
| FPI | 0.19 | 0.18 | 29.3% |
| SPY | 0.98 | — | 14.6% |

Tradable, but a poor risk-adjusted vehicle (Sharpe ~0.2 vs SPY ~1.0), leveraged and illiquid — and
nothing like the 6.6%-vol appraisal index. **FRAGILE.**

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** Appraisal-indexed farmland looks like a real low-beta diversifier (corr to S&P
  −0.13) with a high +8.4%/yr real return and a *positive* inflation loading (+0.66) — but that
  loading is **insignificant** (t = 0.83, 32 yrs), and the only tradable proxies are equity-like
  (beta 0.7–0.9, ~30% vol). Real-economy plausible, literature-supported, statistically unproven on
  the tape → WEAK, not REAL.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** LAND/FPI are real and buyable but small, leveraged, illiquid REITs with
  Sharpe ~0.2; the smooth NCREIF risk profile is unavailable to a retail holder.
- **Smooth & uncorrelated? — BUSTED.** ρ₁ = 0.63 and un-smoothing doubles the vol (6.6% → 13.5%); the
  synthetic control shows appraisal shrinks a true 0.32 beta to ~0.05. The "uncorrelated calm" is a
  measurement illusion, not an asset property.

> **Honesty notes.** Survivorship: only the two surviving listed REITs are in the proxy sample; a
> 12-year, 2-name window is thin. The NCREIF series is a *cited public annual proxy* for the paywalled
> quarterly index — labelled as such, never tuned to a result. One-way costs are charged on NAV; the
> proxies' leverage is a Signal-and-Tradability caveat, not modelled as alpha.
